cards.text: Picture it, friend. The Jews are rebuilding the house of God in Jerusalem. Tattenai, governor of the region west of the Euphrates, has written to King Darius of Persia asking him to check whether King Cyrus ever approved it. So Darius orders a search of the archives stored in the treasury of Babylon.

cards.question: Darius has the archives in Babylon searched for Cyrus's decree. Where does the scroll turn up?

cards.text: Ecbatana, in the province of Media. Somebody tears the whole kitchen apart looking for the scissors, and they were in the OTHER drawer the entire time. Friend, I lived in a junk drawer. I have SEEN this.

cards.question: The scroll is a memo about a decree King Cyrus issued in his first year. Cyrus says to rebuild God's house in Jerusalem as a place for offering ___.
Cyrus's memo even gives the size of God's house: sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide. True or false: the Jews have to pay the building costs themselves.

cards.text: There's one more thing in that memo. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken things from the temple in Jerusalem and carried them off to Babylon.

cards.question: Cyrus's memo says the things Nebuchadnezzar carried off to Babylon must go back to the temple in Jerusalem. What are they?

cards.text: So Darius has his answer, and he writes back to Tattenai, Shethar-bozenai and their officials. Those are the men who went asking the Jews who authorized all this building.

cards.question: King Darius writes to Tattenai, the governor who questioned the Jews about the building. What's the first thing Darius tells him?

answers.text: Stop the work until I come

cards.text: Darius keeps going: "Leave this work on the house of God alone." And the cost? Paid in full from the royal treasury.

cards.question: Darius says the building costs come from the royal treasury, out of the taxes of the provinces west of the ___.

cards.text: Tattenai came out asking questions and walked away with the BILL. His own region's taxes! Friend, you cannot make this up.

cards.question: Darius also orders young bulls, rams and lambs for burnt offerings, plus wheat, salt, wine and oil, whatever the priests in Jerusalem request. They get it ___ without fail.
True or false: Darius says all these supplies let the priests offer sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the lives of the king and his sons.

cards.text: The king's covering the supplies, and he's like, while you're up there, put in a word for me and the boys. Then he adds a warning for anyone who interferes with this decree, and friend, this king does NOT mess around.

cards.question: Darius warns that anyone who interferes with his decree will be impaled on a beam torn from his own house. And what happens to the house?

answers.text: It becomes a pile of rubble

cards.text: Then Darius calls on God, who has caused His Name to dwell there in Jerusalem.

cards.question: Darius asks God to overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter his decree or to do what?

cards.text: Then he signs off: "I, Darius, have issued the decree. Let it be carried out with diligence." Friend, that's not a suggestion. That box is SEALED.
Darius's decree reaches Tattenai, the governor west of the Euphrates, along with Shethar-bozenai and their associates. These are the same men who came asking the Jews who authorized all this.

cards.question: True or false: Tattenai and his associates diligently carry out what King Darius decreed.

cards.text: From asking questions to DILIGENTLY doing what they're told. Friend, I want THAT kind of turnaround on my oven timer. And with the way clear, the Jewish elders build, and they prosper.

cards.question: The Jewish elders build and prosper through the prophesying of two prophets. Who are they?
With Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesying, the elders finish building according to the command of the ___ of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius and Artaxerxes, kings of ___.

cards.text: And then, friend, it happens. The house of God is finished. DONE. COMPLETE. Not almost done. DONE.

cards.question: The temple is completed on the third day of the month of Adar. In which year?

answers.text: The sixth year of King Darius
The first year of King Cyrus

cards.text: The priests, the Levites and the rest of the exiles celebrate the dedication of the house of God with joy. That's me when a whole tray comes out of the oven perfect, except their reason is a WHOLE lot bigger than cookies.

cards.question: For the dedication they offer a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs, plus a sin offering for all Israel of twelve male goats. Why twelve?

answers.text: One for each tribe of Israel
One for each month of the year
One for each gate of Jerusalem

cards.text: With the house dedicated, it's time to get everybody organized. The priests go by their divisions and the Levites by their groups, for the service of God in Jerusalem.

cards.question: True or false: the priests and Levites are organized for the service of God according to King Darius's decree.

cards.text: It's according to what is written in the Book of Moses. Then on the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles keep the Passover.

cards.question: Before the Passover, what had all the priests and Levites done?
The ___ slaughter the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brothers and for themselves.

cards.text: Then comes the Passover meal. After all that building, friend, everybody's ready to eat.

cards.question: True or false: only the Israelites who returned from exile eat the Passover.

cards.text: All who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD eat with them. Then for seven days, they keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy.

cards.question: The people keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy. Where does that joy come from?

cards.text: The LORD had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel. The house of God is standing again, friend. I'm not crying. I just got flour in my eye.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'Picture it, friend.' / 'The Jews are rebuilding…' / 'Tattenai… has written to King Darius…' / 'So Darius orders a search…'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The card states facts from the previous passage: Tattenai wrote to Darius asking him to check whether Cyrus approved the rebuilding (Ezra 5:6-17). The card cites only Ezra 6:1, so those facts have no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'Ecbatana, in the province of Media.' / 'Somebody tears the whole kitchen apart…' / 'Friend, I lived in a junk drawer.' / 'I have SEEN this.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'Those are the men who went asking the Jews who authorized all this building' comes from Ezra 5:3-4, outside the passage. The card cites only Ezra 6:6, so the fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The blank asks for 'Euphrates' in 'provinces west of the ___'. Card 1 already told the baker that Tattenai is 'governor of the region west of the Euphrates', so the answer is given away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card is only a reaction joke about the answer to card 11. It tells no new part of the passage. It also has three sentences.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: 'Then Darius calls on God' renames what the text does. Ezra 6:12 is a wish: 'May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there, overthrow…'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: 'Darius asks God to overthrow any king or people…' calls Darius's words a request. Ezra 6:12 words them as 'May God… overthrow…'. This is the same pattern as the Naomi example the rule marks wrong.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: The story card runs past two sentences: the two-sentence quote, then 'Friend, that's not a suggestion.' and 'That box is SEALED.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card mostly recaps stop 1: Tattenai's title, Shethar-bozenai and their associates, and 'the same men who came asking the Jews' (already said on stop 1 card 8). 'The decree reaches Tattenai' isn't in Ezra 6:13. The card doesn't move the passage forward.

The joke compares officials who went from questioning to diligently obeying with a 'turnaround on my oven timer'. An oven timer doesn't question or obey anything, so the action doesn't match and the line reads as 'huh?'

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: 'From asking questions to DILIGENTLY doing what they're told.' / 'Friend, I want THAT kind of turnaround on my oven timer.' / 'And with the way clear, the Jewish elders build, and they prosper.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The second blank asks for 'Persia' in 'kings of ___'. Stop 1 card 1 already called him 'King Darius of Persia', so the answer is given away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences: 'The LORD had turned the heart…' / 'The house of God is standing again, friend.' / 'I'm not crying.' / 'I just got flour in my eye.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
